written.myAnswer: Gaseous exchange in plants occurs by diffusion. In leaves and young stems, gases pass through stomata; in woody stems, they pass through lenticels. Roots exchange gases with the air in the soil through their surface. Within the plant, gases move between cells and the air spaces. During the day, leaves take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis and release oxygen; plants also respire. At night, photosynthesis stops but respiration continues, so plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide.
